thread:
lina-support: Heads up — multiple customers hitting 5xx / timeouts on hosted inference since ~10:02 UTC. Tickets inbound: #C-9182, #C-9184. Error rate spike on /v1/generate. Anyone already looking?

omar-eng-infra: I'm seeing connection errors to our prefix cache cluster (redis-primary). Metrics show connection_timeouts and client-side timeouts. Putting logs below.

omar-eng-infra: ```
2026-02-28T10:01:57Z runtime-worker-7b9f ERROR request_id=aa1b2c redis.exceptions.TimeoutError: Timeout connecting to 10.12.4.23:6379 after 5000ms
2026-02-28T10:02:01Z api-gateway-5 ERROR downstream timeout request_id=aa1b2c elapsed=60000ms status=504
2026-02-28T10:03:04Z runtime-worker-7b9f ERROR prefix-cache fetch failed key="prefix:abcd1234" err="ERR max number of clients reached"
```

maya-eng-runtime: That log looks like the prefix/KV layer is blocking requests while it waits for Redis. We rely on that cache for prefix KV to avoid recompute; if it's blocking we can get head-of-line latencies that cascade into 504s.

elena-cs: Customers reporting "request failed with 500" and timeouts, some are in prod. One asked if this is a billing issue. (cc @billing-bot)

billing-bot: Billing unaffected — metric pipeline still ingesting.

lina-support: OK escalate. @tony-oncall can you take infra action? We should also prepare mitigation steps to reduce customer impact (fall back to uncached path or toggle cache).

tony-oncall: On it. First I want to confirm cluster health. Omar — can you run redis-cli info and memstat on the primaries? Also check eviction and connected_clients.

omar-eng-infra: Ran quick check, pub:

redis-primary-1> INFO replication
role:master
connected_slaves:0

redis-primary-1> INFO clients
connected_clients: 1025
maxclients: 1024

Looks like we hit maxclients, causing new connections to be refused -> client timeouts. We're also seeing slow commands pile up.

maya-eng-runtime: That's consistent. The runtime opens a connection per request to prefix cache (legacy). When clients get refused the client lib waits for timeout and the worker blocks. We need a short-term toggle to prevent blocking access to cache and go direct to compute path (slower per-request, but avoids 5xx).

lina-support: Any quick config to flip? We can coordinate config change + rolling restart if needed.

maya-eng-runtime: Yes — add env var RUNTIME_DISABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true to runtime-worker and rollout. Code checks this flag and will skip prefix cache reads/writes. That path is used in canary but not prod by default.

omar-eng-infra: I'll scale up redis-primary and bounce one node to clear stuck connections. But we should do the toggle first to stop more blocked workers. Tony — can you run the rollout?

tony-oncall: Doing the toggle now (will push env with zero-downtime deploy and 30s pod grace). Command: 

kubectl -n inference set env deployment/runtime-worker RUNTIME_DISABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true && kubectl rollout status deployment/runtime-worker -n inference

Starting at 10:12 UTC.

kevin-srebot: Alert: prefix_cache_error_count > 300/s for 10m — auto-escalation triggered.

lina-support: Notifying affected customers with ETA ~10-20m mitigation window. Posting to status page.

omar-eng-infra: Scaling redis-primary statefulset from 3 -> 5 replicas and will increase maxclients to 4096 on the nodes. Patching redis configmap now.

maya-eng-runtime: After toggle we should see request timeouts drop. We'll monitor request latency and 5xx. Also adding fallback circuit to avoid synchronous writes to prefix cache during high latency. That will be a short PR (non-urgent) but might take hours.

[10:21 UTC] tony-oncall: Rollout succeeded. runtime-worker pods are back with RUNTIME_DISABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true.

[10:24 UTC] omar-eng-infra: Redis rolling update in progress. Increased maxclients applied. Old connections cleared on nodes that restarted.

[10:28 UTC] kevin-srebot: Alerts: 5xx rate for /v1/generate dropping from 12% -> 1.4% over last 5m. Timeouts falling.

lina-support: Good. I'm updating tickets: told customers we applied mitigation (disabled prefix cache) and are working on durable fix (scale and config). Requested confirmation if any customers still seeing failures.

elena-cs: Customer C-9184 reports reduced errors, still occasional 500s about 1 in 200. They accepted we disabled cache and want ETA for full fix.

omar-eng-infra: Redis cluster is green. New connected_clients: 420. No more ERR max number of clients. Reconnected workers should be able to reach cache if re-enabled later.

maya-eng-runtime: Next steps: 1) Code change to switch cache access to non-blocking (async) with connection pooling — PR opened MM-1245. 2) Improve telemetry to alert earlier on connection saturation. 3) Add defensive client-side max retries with fast-fail.

lina-support: Can we get an ETA on PR + rollout?

maya-eng-runtime: PR targeting end of day, review + canary ~3-4h after merge, full rollout tomorrow morning depending on reviews. Will update thread.

tony-oncall: Postmortem pointers: track customers impacted, exact time window 10:02-10:30 UTC, root cause: redis client saturation (maxclients) causing connection refused/timeouts -> runtime blocking -> 504/5xx. Mitigations applied: disable prefix cache, scale redis, increase maxclients. Long-term: change client behavior and add circuit breakers.

elena-cs: I'll send follow-up emails summarizing mitigation and timeline. Include note that billing unaffected.

lina-support: Closing loop: status page updated, customers notified, tickets updated. Leaving this thread open until PR merges and we re-enable prefix cache.

kevin-srebot: Post-incident metric snapshot: 5xx rate baseline 0.3% -> peak 13% at 10:05 -> back to baseline by 10:40.

lina-support: Thanks all. If anyone re-enables cache later, please coordinate with infra and run a dark canary first (5% traffic).

maya-eng-runtime: Will coordinate. Will also add guard in runtime to refuse to enable prefix cache if redis connected_clients > 800.

tony-oncall: Marking incident as mitigated. Will start formal postmortem doc after PR lands.

lina-support: Notifying stakeholders and closing tickets pending customer ack. Great response everyone. :thumbsup:
